Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
Oral Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 02.03.2017 passed in M.V.C.No.1197/2012 by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Mandya ('the Tribunal' for short) questioning the quantum of compensation and the liability fastened against the owner of the vehicle.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Heard the arguments of Sri P. Nataraju, the learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri B.C.
Shivanne Gowda, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
Sri Ranganathaprasad B.S., the learned counsel for the owner of the vehicle is absent.
During the course of the argument, the learned counsel for the petitioner has restricted the appeal to the extent of liability and hence the quantum of compensation is not examined.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that on the date of the accident, the vehicle in question was having a temporary permit to ply on the route where the accident occurred.
The petitioner was unable to place the same before the Tribunal.
The owner of the vehicle did not assist the Tribunal for effective adjudication regarding liability.
6. Now the petitioner has filed I.A.No.1/2017 under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC by producing the letter issued by the Assistant Regional Transport Officer, Bagepalli and also the extract of the permit.
This goes to show that the vehicle in question was having a temporary permit between 11.06.2012 to 10.07.2012.
But the same was not brought to the notice of the Tribunal.
In this appeal, the owner is also silent and there is no representation though appeared through his advocate.

The evidence on S J Nidhi vs Ravi Mogili on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183160299/
2 record goes to show that on the NC: 2024:KHC:37710 date of the accident, the vehicle was plying at the place of accident in breach of permit.

sentences.text:
7. The Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in M.F.A.No.4516/2014 and other connected cases dated 15.07.2022, referring to the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of RANI AND OTHERS v.
NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 8 SCC 492, held that the breach of terms and conditions of the policy is not a fundamental breach within the meaning of Sections 149(2)(a)(i)(a) and (c) and Sections 66 and 2(31) of he Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and recover it from the owner of the vehicle.
8.

entities.text:
RANI AND OTHERS v.
NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 8 SCC 492
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The facts of the said case is aptly applicable to the case on hand.

If the owner of the vehicle is able to convince the Insurance Company that he had a valid permit to ply the vehicle at the time of the accident, it is between the owner and the Insurance Company to settle their differences.
Hence, it is a case for applying the principles of pay and recovery.

Accordingly, appeal as well as I.A.No.1/2017 merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER (i) I.A.No.1/2017 filed by the petitioner is allowed.
(ii) The appeal is allowed in part.
(iii) The impugned judgment and award is modified to the extent of liability only.
(iv) The liability is on the owner of the vehicle to pay the compensation.

(v) The Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation with interest within eight weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in the same proceedings.

SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE MD S J Nidhi vs Ravi Mogili on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183160299/
